contextUsed.text:
=== GLOBAL STANDARDS (L1) ===
principles:
  typescript:
    strict_mode: true
    target: ES2022
    no_any: "Avoid `any` — use `unknown` with type guards or explicit generics"
    async_first: "All DB calls, LLM calls, and I/O are async — always await"

  error_handling:
    pattern: "AppError class hierarchy with immutable HTTP status codes"
    subclasses: [ValidationError 400, AuthError 401, ForbiddenError 403, NotFoundError 404, ConflictError 409, UnprocessableError 422]
    serialization: "{ error: string, code?: string, details?: Record<string, unknown> }"
    rule: "Throw from route handlers; centralized errorHandler middleware catches and serializes"

  database:
    driver: "pg Pool (async, connection pooling)"
    helpers: "query<T>() returns T[], queryOne<T>() returns T|undefined, execute() returns { rowCount }"
    placeholders: "$1, $2, ... (numbered, NOT positional ?)"
    transactions: "transaction<T>(fn) wraps in BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK"
    migrations: "SQL files in pg-migrations/, timestamp prefix YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for new files, tracked in schema_migrations"
    slow_query_logging: "Queries > 500ms logged with sanitized params"

  validation:
    library: zod
    pattern: "Middleware factories — validateBody(schema), validateQuery(schema), validateParams(schema)"
    method: "safeParse (not .parse() which throws)"
    response: "{ error: firstIssueMessage, details: zodError.issues }"

  llm:
    return_type: "ChatResult { text: string, usage: { inputTokens, outputTokens } }"
    rule: "Always use .text accessor — never treat ChatResult as a string"
    providers: "Multi-provider routing via model registry — claude-cli, anthropic, openai-compat, openrouter"

  api_design:
    documentation: "JSDoc @swagger annotations on every route → auto-generated OpenAPI spec"
    pagination: "{ items: T[], total: number, hasMore: boolean, cursor?: string }"
    response_shape: "Success: res.json(data). Error: { error, code, details } via AppError"
    middleware_chain: "validateBody(schema) → authRequired → async handler"
    security_headers: "helmet (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, noSniff, referrerPolicy)"
    caching: "Cache-Control: no-store on all responses, etag: false"

  testing:
    backend: "Jest with ts-jest, serial (maxWorkers: 1), 30s timeout, PG_POOL_SIZE=1"
    frontend: "Vitest with jsdom, globals: true"
    rule: "Always clean up DB pool connections in afterAll()"

  code_style:
    no_over_engineering: "Only make changes that are directly requested or clearly necessary"
    no_premature_abstraction: "Three similar lines > premature helper function"
    minimal_containers: "Don't add docstrings, comments, or type annotations to code you didn't change"
    security_first: "Never commit .env files, API keys, or secrets. Use vault for sensitive values."

=== PROJECT CONTEXT (L3) ===
name: rorca
type: web-app
purpose: AI spec orchestration platform that converts plain-English briefs into structured user story specs and autonomously executes them story-by-story via isolated agent subprocesses (claude, opencode, or codex)

stack:
  - React 18
  - TypeScript 5.7 (strict)
  - Vite 5
  - Tailwind CSS 3
  - xterm.js (@xterm/xterm)
  - react-router-dom 7
  - framer-motion
  - recharts
  - Express.js
  - PostgreSQL 16 (pg pool, pgvector, Apache AGE)
  - pg-boss (job queue)
  - Node.js >= 20
  - tsx (TypeScript runner)
  - Jest (backend tests)
  - Vitest (frontend tests)
  - Playwright (E2E)

key_modules:
  - src/panels/ — 5 primary UI panels (Specs, Runs, Analytics, Direction, Settings)
  - src/components/ — shared UI (Sidebar, RunTerminal, CommandPalette, slide-overs)
  - src/contexts/ — WorkspaceContext, AuthContext, ThemeContext, ToastContext
  - backend/src/routes/ — 32 Express route files
  - backend/src/lib/ — core services (sse-hub, direction-stack, llm-client, execution-engine, context-router, workspace-echolocation, rate-limiter, scheduler)
  - backend/src/worker.ts — pg-boss worker process (pipeline job consumer)
  - backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts — sole execution engine for all agent types
  - backend/src/db/ — PostgreSQL pool, migration runner, 70+ migrations
  - backend/src/mcp/ — MCP stdio server (24 tools)
  - forge/ — spec JSON files, run-loop.sh bash fallback, self-register script

constraints:
  - Migrations must use timestamp format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for new files (sequential 001-079 already exist)
  - Worker process must be running for pipeline triggers to execute
  - AGE search_path must be restored after every graph query
  - Auth middleware is globally disabled (intentional, local tool)
  - CLAUDE_BIN full path required for child process spawning (NVM PATH not inherited)
  - spec id is always the filename slug, never the human title

deployment_target: local (self-hosted, npm run dev) or Docker Compose

ports:
  frontend: 5210
  backend: 3030
  finops_sim: 5200

integrations:
  - claude CLI (claude --print)
  - opencode CLI (opencode run)
  - codex CLI (codex --approval-mode auto-edit)
  - GitHub OAuth + webhooks
  - Linear (post-launch)
  - Vercel (post-launch)
  - Slack (post-launch)
  - Stripe billing

=== SPEC BRIEF (L4) ===
Fix 5 bugs in the wave-parallel Run View UI:

BUG 1 — Wave label mismatch (RunStoryList.tsx):
The frontend's compileWavesFromStories() filters out already-passed stories before running topological sort, then re-indexes waves starting at 0 from the remaining stories. The execution engine labels waves at startup from the full DAG (Wave 0, Wave 1, Wave 2...). Result: the right-side story list shows "Wave 0" for what the engine calls "Wave 2", confusing users.
Fix: store wave_index on story_results rows (the execution engine already emits wave_index in WAL events via waveIndex field). The frontend should read wave_index from story data rather than recomputing topology client-side. For stories not yet started (no story_result row), fall back to the client-side topo sort but offset by the highest known wave_index so numbering stays consistent.

BUG 2 — Missing terminal for wave-blocked stories (MiniTerminalPane / RunViewPanel):
Stories in Wave N+1 that are waiting for Wave N to finish its merge do not get a MiniTerminalPane rendered at all. The frontend only renders terminals for stories that have started (have a WAL story_started event). The result is that a story visually disappears from the left panel even though it is clearly queued and the user expects to see it waiting.
Fix: render a MiniTerminalPane in 'waiting' status for all stories in the current run's spec, not just started ones. The pane should show a subtle "Waiting for wave merge..." placeholder until story_started fires. This matches how the right-side story list already shows all stories.

BUG 3 — Semantic steps lost on story completion (MiniTerminalPane):
Semantic steps (tool calls, reasoning steps, bash commands) are accumulated in React useState from live semantic_step SSE events. When a story completes, the SSE stream closes. If the MiniTerminalPane component unmounts and remounts (which happens when wave state changes cause a re-render of the parent), steps resets to [] and the semantic log shows "No semantic data" for the completed story.
Fix: persist semantic_step events to the database in a new run_semantic_steps table (run_id, story_id, sequence INT, type TEXT, label TEXT, created_at). The /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/stories/:storyId/stream SSE endpoint should replay persisted semantic steps on connect (same pattern as run_output_chunks for raw terminal). The backend execution engine emits semantic steps via WAL or direct DB insert. On reconnect or remount, the frontend receives full history.

BUG 4 — Markdown not rendered in sub-terminals (MiniTerminalPane):
The main RunTerminal.tsx has a markdownToHtml() function (line 127) that converts **bold**, ### headers, `code`, and bullet lists into HTML before passing to ansi-to-html. MiniTerminalPane.tsx only uses ansi-to-html directly, so raw markdown syntax renders as literal characters (**text**, ### header) in the sub-terminal raw view.
Fix: extract markdownToHtml() from RunTerminal.tsx into a shared utility (src/lib/markdownToHtml.ts). Apply it in MiniTerminalPane's chunk processing pipeline before ansi-to-html, using the same HTML_LINE_PREFIX sentinel pattern already used in RunTerminal to avoid double-escaping.

BUG 5 — No expand/fullscreen for sub-terminals (MiniTerminalPane):
Sub-terminals are fixed height with no way to see more output. For long-running stories or stories with extensive output, the user cannot read the terminal without switching to the full run view. The main RunTerminal has full scroll, but MiniTerminalPane does not expose an expand control.
Fix: add an expand icon button (Maximize2 from lucide-react) to the MiniTerminalPane header. Clicking it opens a modal overlay (full viewport, dark background) that renders the same MiniTerminalPane content at full size with proper scrolling. The modal supports Escape to close and preserves the raw/semantic mode toggle. The expanded view uses the same SSE stream — no duplicate connections (share the parent component state via props or context).

Each story must include:
- TypeScript type check passing (npx tsc --noEmit) with zero new errors
- The fix verified against the described scenario (e.g. wave labels consistent between left and right panel, semantic steps survive component remount, markdown renders correctly in sub-terminal, expand modal opens and closes)
- No regressions to existing sequential (non-wave) run behavior
